item.title: 'Cortisol Level' Memes Flood Social Media In Wide Array Of Jokes And Edits
item.description: Cortisol Spike or Cortisol Level is a slang phrase and reaction image or GIF format used to humorously describe moments of sudden stress, shock, second-hand embarrassment or psychological discomfort that stem from the release of cortisol, the body's main stress hormone. The meme typically uses an image of a cortisol level meter graphic labeled from "Low" to "High," with the needle pointing toward the end that fits the situation. item.title: 'Despicable Me' Gets Remixed With Israel In Viral 'Big Yahu' Memes
item.description: The Big Yahu is a nickname for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, most commonly used in memes on TikTok and Instagram Reels. The nickname was popularized in mid-January 2026 by TikToker @gassygoontoonx, who used footage of Gru from Despicable Me as Big Yahu. The nickname became the further subject of ironic memes over the following weeks, some of which paint Netanyahu as a great leader. item.title: How “An IQ Too High?” Became a Meme
item.description: An IQ Too High? is a reaction image and exploitable meme depicting an image of a crow accompanied with the text "AN IQ TOO HIGH?" The image originates from a video thumbnail by the YouTube channel Real Science, which was uploaded in 2022. In late 2026 and early 2026, the thumbnail spread online as a reaction meme, primarily in TikTok comment sections as a sticker. item.title: Who Is This Dinosaur and Why is He Dressed Like a Divorced Dad? The Redneck Baby Sinclair Meme Explained
item.description: Redneck Baby Sinclair is a reaction image and exploitable meme featuring the character Baby Sinclair from the 90’s American family sitcom Dinosaurs. The meme, primarily found on X/Twitter, depicts the baby dinosaur in various outfits, scenarios, and environments associated with "Redneck" stereotypes.

item.title: VTuber Inugami Korone's Catchphrase 'Water In The Fire Why?' Continues Generating Memes Online
item.description: Water In The Fire Why? refers to an Engrish catchphrase said by Hololive virtual YouTuber talent Inugami Korone in a clip while she's playing Super Mario Bros., in which she wonders how the fire bar obstacle is still burning while it's underwater. Her reaction became the subject of animations and other memes among the community in the 2020s.
